method: Finite primal optimizer-face reconstruction, residual-cut proof for real capacities, rectangular-tail counting and explicit exact boundary witnesses; no native scientific execution.

universal_hand_checks.derivation: Full binary tree has2^(H+1)-1=4k-1 vertices. A descendant leaf set of size k_e carries k*k_e distinct cross-root unit commodities. Doubled loads force C_e>=2k*k_e separately; equality is feasible and any larger component strictly increases positive linear cost.

Every internal edge load is sum of the row loads or column loads below it. Individual terminal bounds2k imply internal bound2k*k_e; necessity follows from terminal edges. Nonnegative admitted demand and cross-root unique paths are essential.

universal_hand_checks.item: Real-capacity cut import without algorithm-termination assumption
universal_hand_checks.derivation: A maximum flow exists by compactness of a finite bounded feasible polytope. If its residual graph had a positive-capacity s-t path, augment by the positive minimum along this finite path. Otherwise reachable vertices form a cut with all outgoing edges saturated and incoming flows zero, giving flow=cut capacity. This proves the exact finite real-valued import without assuming integer capacities or termination of a naive augmenting algorithm.

Source-side left A/right B gives2k(k-|A|)+sum_(A x (R\B))d+2k|B|, exactly the printed formula. Every active slope is a subset sum of nonnegative X, in[0,S]. A finite minimum has right derivative the least active slope; no missing tie convention.

Full offered feasibility makes y=d the only matrix with the offered total, since every coordinate is upper-bounded. Strict terminal slack sums to strict slack at every physical edge. At F=2k^2 every row and every column must attain2k in every optimizer, so every internal descendant sum saturates too. The event is uniform over all optimal matrices, not a preferred solver output.

Direct exponential integral gives E exp(lambda X)=1/(1-lambda) for lambda<1. Independence gives power n; Markov with lambda=1-1/a gives exp(-n(a-1-log a)), also with negative lambda for the lower tail. Derivatives of I(1/(1-delta)) and I(1/(1+delta)) are delta/(1-delta)^2 and delta/(1+delta)^2, respectively. Integration gives delta^2/2 and delta^2/8 for0<delta<1.

At2-delta each offered terminal load is k+(1-delta)Gamma(k,1). A2k union bound gives2k exp(-k delta^2/2)=2k^-31 at the printed delta. Strict endpoint slack also holds in a positive right neighborhood for each finite realization; this is required for r=1 at the endpoint. Monotonic demands give all earlier times.
Only a+d>k matters. Failure of a rectangle cut implies Z<ad/(1+delta), since ad-k(a+d-k)=(k-a)(k-d)>=0. Thus failure probability<=exp(-c ad), c>=delta^2/8. Different cuts can be dependent.

Let q=min(a,d),ell=k-max(a,d), so0<=ell<q. For q<=k/2, orientation and binomial choices give at most2q k^(2q) over ell; area>=qk/2. For q>k/2, area>k^2/4 and all subset pairs are at most4^k. At c>=8log(k)/k these give sum_(q>=1)2q k^-2q=2k^-2/(1-k^-2)^2 and(4/k^2)^k exactly. The high endpoint plus increasing demand holds for all later times.

E[S/k^2]=1, Var[S/k^2]=k^-2. Away from2 the same good event applies eventually. At2 squeeze k^2+(1-delta)S<=F(2)<=2k^2. This proves throughput convergence without interchanging a derivative limit. Summable dyadic failure bounds imply eventual good events under any common coupling by the first Borel-Cantelli argument.

exact_controls.assumptions: Any dyadic k and deterministic all slopes x>0; algebraic diagnostic, not an independent Exp sample.
exact_controls.calculation: Feasible y_ij=min(1+(t-1)x,2) attains the offered/terminal upper bound, so F=k^2 min(1+(t-1)x,2). S=k^2 x. Right marginal is1 below t*=1+1/x and0 at/above; every edge is saturated at equality.

exact_controls.purpose: Nonunique optimizer/spare graph and realized-slope normalization
exact_controls.assumptions: k=2, t=2, X=[[3,3],[1/2,1/2]], all slopes positive.
exact_controls.calculation: d=[[4,4],[3/2,3/2]]. F=7 via row1 total4,row2 total3. Optimizers y=[[a,4-a],[3/2,3/2]] for3/2<=a<=5/2. At a=2 only one leaf edge is saturated and M=6 of N=7; at a=5/2 two leaf edges are saturated and M=5. Near t=2, F=t+5, so F'_+=1 and r=1/7, not1/4. This is allowed inside the transition and outside the asymptotic delta<1 range.

exact_controls.purpose: All-cut feasibility cannot be replaced by terminal offered-load tests
exact_controls.calculation: All offered row loads are>8 and all column loads>8, yet A={1,2,3},D={1,2} has rectangle demand33/5<8=2k(a+d-k). The associated cut is24+33/5=153/5<32. Thus high saturation is impossible on this input despite all terminal offered loads exceeding capacity. This validates the need for the all-cuts argument, not a counterexample to the claimed large-k probability bound.

exact_controls.purpose: Independence is an actual assumption, not merely exponential marginals
exact_controls.calculation: Each marginal still has the same Exp law/stream mean and quadratic variance, but F/k^2=min(1+(t-1)X,2) and the switch1+1/X remains random. At a fixed1<t<2 the saturated probability is exp(-1/(t-1))>0 independent of k, so the claimed concentration fails without independence.

At t=1 all demands1 and every edge has half its designed capacity load, so full tree spare for all k. k=2,4,...256 have delta>=1 and are outside the window theorem; k=512 is the first dyadic with64log(k)<k. Zero design prices would destroy uniqueness; d=0/no-vertex or general rerouting conventions are not part of this model.
